title: Personal release pin and canary scratchpad
content:
Scratchpad: release pin + canary thoughts

Goal: ship model-serving runtime changes with minimal user impact. This is my personal checklist and running notes. Not final.

High-level plan
- Pin runtime image: rw-runtime:v2026-03-rc3 -> rw-runtime:v2026-03 (target)
- Canary split: start 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% (holdpoints at 1h, 4h, 12h)
- Metric gates: p95 inference latency delta <= +15%, token error rate <= 0.2%, increase in 5xx rate <= 0.1%
- Rollback triggers: any sustained SLO breach for 30m or critical errors impacting >0.5% of requests

Canary config notes
- Use route tag 'canary:mc-v2026-03' for tracking
- k8s rollout: use Deployment with 5 replicas in canary pool; service split via envoy header-route
- Feature flags: make sure 'kv-cache-forward-merge' is disabled during canary to isolate changes
- Model pinning: ensure requests use model_id=redwood/gptx-2@v3.2-q4_0 (explicit to avoid auto-upgrades)

Checklist (quick)
- [ ] Build rw-runtime:v2026-03 and push to registry
- [ ] Create canary route in API gateway + label tracing
- [ ] Update console rollout UI (notes) and link to this doc
- [ ] Run smoke tests (ml-eval quickset + sample chat flows)
- [ ] Deploy canary at 1% (monitor for 1h)
- [ ] If OK -> move to 5% and run extended load test
- [ ] Update team Slack #sre and #serving with progress messages
- [ ] On success -> 20% for 12h, then 100% with final rollout annotation
- [ ] Tag release in github and add Confluence note

Monitoring queries / alerts
- p99 latency (last 5m) by route: query: avg_over_time(latency_p99[5m])
- Error rate: sum(5xx)/sum(total) over 5m windows
- Model output diffs: run quick eval harness comparing canary vs baseline using prompt-suite A
- Cost delta: token_cost_per_minute compare canary vs control

Open questions / TODOs
- Is the canary scaling policy tested with our autoscaler? (check job: AS-231)
- Do we want to isolate stateful KV caches per canary shard? Pros: safer; Cons: loses cache hits -> cost blips
- Compute budget: Dedicated nodes limited this week; coordinate with infra to reserve 2 GPUs on us-west-2
- Notify customers on Dedicated tiers? Only if we plan >5% traffic or a scheduled maintenance window

Commands I ran
- docker build -t registry/rw-runtime:v2026-03 -f infra/Dockerfile.runtime .
- kubectl -n canary set image deployment/rw-runtime rw-runtime=registry/rw-runtime:v2026-03
- curl -s -H 'x-canary:mc-v2026-03' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health

Notes for postmortem template
- timeline: when traffic shifted and when anomaly started
- relevant traces: request ids (prefixed rw-canary-) and sampling of failed payloads
- metric deltas: pre/post thin-client and heavy-client splits

Quick links
- Git PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rw-infra/pull/482
- Jira: JIRA-RELEASE-1293
- Canary dashboards: /dashboards/rw/canary/mc-v2026-03

Personal thoughts
- Keep the first canary small and instrument more than usual. If the perf regression is subtle it will show in 95/99 rather than mean.
- Prefer an explicit model pin over automatic aliasing; easier to reason about regressions.

End of scratchpad (Maya)
